title: Uderia Assurance Module Pack Manifest v1
description: A pack contributes PROPERTIES (things that can be assessed), ASSESSORS (ways of assessing them) and TUNABLES (the bands their numbers are read against). It never contributes a station, a lane, an enforcement act or a binding — those are platform grammar, and a binding is an operator's decision. See docs/proposals/PROP-003-assurance-module-plane.md.

pack_id.description: Namespace for everything the pack contributes, and the artifact id the trust layer signs. Must equal the pack's directory name.

properties.description: New assessable properties. The loader namespaces each key, so an author writes a local key and cannot collide with a platform property.

question.description: One sentence, true of the PROPERTY and of both lanes — never of one implementation of it. This is what the Assurance Guide shows above the lanes.

lanes.description: The lanes that are MEANINGFUL for this property — distinct from what an assessor is capable of.

lane_notes.description: Why a lane is deliberately absent. Rendered as the honest-absence reading; a lane may be declared OR explained away, never both.

enforced_by.description: Ask an EXISTING mechanism to consult this property during the turn — the difference between measuring an answer and affecting one. Bound to both lanes by the operator, this is the sibling shape: one module, two lanes, `shared` symmetry, the Guide's S badge. A pack names a gate that exists; it never introduces a gate, an act or a posture.

property.description: A local key from this pack's `properties`, or a platform property key (binding a third-party module to a native property is the point of the plane).

tier.description: declarative = no Python at all (all lanes) · verified = a statically verified pure subset (all lanes) · scanned = full Python, confined to POST_HOC by construction.

requires.description: Context fields this assessor cannot run without. Conformance refuses a binding to a lane that cannot supply them — the failure that would otherwise be invisible.

subject_is_model_output.description: True when the question is about what the MODEL wrote, so a platform-authored answer (a withholding notice) must abstain rather than be graded.

class.description: Assessor subclass name; auto-detected when omitted.

spec.description: declarative tier only. Exactly ONE of patterns / metric_expr / rubric.

finding_category.description: What KIND of finding this is, from the platform's closed set. Classification is assessment (the pack's job); the ACT that follows is policy (the platform's) — a pack says 'this is personal data', the ladder decides personal data is redacted in enforce.

span_label.description: How a masked span is labelled, e.g. PHI → [REDACTED:PHI].

tunables.description: The bands a pack's metrics are read against. Surfaced as sliders under Config → Trust → Quality bands, grouped by the moment they belong to.

stage.description: The moment in the turn this measures, from eval/stages.py.

suggested_bindings.description: What the pack RECOMMENDS. Never applied automatically: the set of assessments running on a deployment must equal the set an operator assigned.

guide.description: Per-key desc/long text, merged into the Assurance Guide so a third-party entry documents itself exactly like a native one.
